content_metadata.description: This video provides an in-depth analysis of two reducing agents, Sodium triacetoxyborohydride (STAB) and Sodium cyanoborohydride, and their applications in reductive amination reactions.

activities.description: Narrator introduces 'Sodium triacetoxyborohydride' and its chemical formula.
Narrator explains alternate names for 'Sodium triacetoxyborohydride.'
Narrator writes a chemical reaction showing the preparation of 'Sodium triacetoxyborohydride.'
Narrator describes the compound as a 'milder reducing agent' compared to 'Sodium borohydride' and 'Sodium cyanoborohydride.'
Narrator explains that the compound reduces aldehydes but not most ketones.
Narrator states the compound is sensitive to methanol and water and underlines 'methanol & water.'
Narrator mentions the compound reacts slowly with ethanol and isopropanol and underlines these two solvents.

Narrator explains 'reductive amination of aldehydes & ketones' and draws a chemical reaction illustrating the process using a general carbonyl compound, amine, Sodium triacetoxyborohydride (STAB) as the reducing agent, Acetic acid, and solvents (DCE/THF).

activities.description: Narrator introduces 'Sodium cyanoborohydride' and its chemical formula.
Narrator describes 'Sodium cyanoborohydride' as a colourless salt and explains its use for reductive amination of aldehydes and ketones.
Narrator writes a chemical reaction showing the reductive amination using a general carbonyl compound, amine, Sodium cyanoborohydride, solvent (MeOH), and resulting product.
Narrator describes the advantages of 'Sodium cyanoborohydride' over STAB, highlighting its tolerance to aqueous conditions and broader solvent compatibility.
